question: What was net realized revenue in May 2026?

input.sql:
SELECT o.order_id, o.gross_amount, o.discount_amount, o.gross_amount - o.discount_amount AS net_order, p.amount, p.status, p.payment_date, o.order_date
FROM orders o
JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
LIMIT 20;

SELECT r.refund_id, r.payment_id, r.refund_amount, r.refund_date, p.order_id, p.amount, p.status, p.payment_date
FROM refunds r
JOIN payments p ON p.payment_id = r.payment_id
LIMIT 20;

SELECT SUM(o.gross_amount - o.discount_amount) AS net_settled_may
FROM orders o
JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE p.payment_date >= '2026-05-01' AND p.payment_date < '2026-06-01'
  AND p.status = 'settled';

SELECT 
  COUNT(*) AS total_payments,
  AVG(DATEDIFF('day', o.order_date, p.payment_date)) AS avg_lag_days,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY DATEDIFF('day', o.order_date, p.payment_date)) AS p95_lag
FROM payments p
JOIN orders o ON p.order_id = o.order_id;

SELECT MAX(DATEDIFF('day', o.order_date, p.payment_date)) AS max_lag,
       MIN(DATEDIFF('day', o.order_date, p.payment_date)) AS min_lag
FROM payments p
JOIN orders o ON p.order_id = o.order_id;
SELECT p.status, COUNT(*) FROM payments p GROUP BY p.status;

SELECT SUM(o.gross_amount - o.discount_amount) AS net_settled_orders_may
FROM orders o
JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-05-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-06-01'
  AND p.status = 'settled';

SELECT 
  SUM(p.amount) AS sum_payment_amount,
  SUM(o.gross_amount - o.discount_amount) AS sum_net_order
FROM payments p
JOIN orders o ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE p.status = 'settled';

SELECT 
  COUNT(*) AS cnt,
  AVG(r.refund_amount) AS avg_refund,
  AVG(p.amount) AS avg_payment
FROM refunds r
JOIN payments p ON r.payment_id = p.payment_id;

question: How is net realized revenue defined in the current version?

input.sql:
SELECT o.order_id, o.gross_amount, o.discount_amount, o.gross_amount - o.discount_amount AS net_order, p.amount, p.status
FROM orders o
JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
LIMIT 20;

SELECT r.refund_id, r.payment_id, r.refund_amount, p.amount, p.status, o.order_id
FROM refunds r
JOIN payments p ON r.payment_id = p.payment_id
JOIN orders o ON p.order_id = o.order_id
LIMIT 20;

SELECT p.payment_id, p.status, p.amount, COUNT(r.refund_id) as refund_count, SUM(r.refund_amount) as total_refunded
FROM payments p
LEFT JOIN refunds r ON r.payment_id = p.payment_id
GROUP BY p.payment_id, p.status, p.amount
HAVING refund_count > 0
LIMIT 20;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payments p JOIN refunds r ON r.payment_id = p.payment_id WHERE p.status = 'settled';
SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'main';
SELECT status, COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM payments GROUP BY status;
SELECT SUM(refund_amount) FROM refunds;

input.answer_text: Net realized revenue in the current governed definition is the payment-level amount that has actually been realized: sum of payments.amount where payments.status = 'settled' – which by construction equals orders.gross_amount – orders.discount_amount, the order-level discount applied – recognized on payments.payment_date. Payments with status pending_settlement, failed, chargeback, voided or refunded do not count as revenue, and refunds are tracked separately in the refunds table with refund_date recognition and partial refund_amounts allowed; e.g., a payment that later ends refunded is excluded from revenue.
